abstract.para: The Linux kernel's scheduler allocates processor execution time to running threads according to process-level CPU scheduling policies.

topic.para: The Linux kernel scheduler can use the following policies:

listitem.para: First In, First Out: A running thread continues executing until it blocks on an I/O request, explicitly yields execution, or is preempted by a higher-priority real-time thread. Priority levels range from 1 (lowest) to 99 (highest).
Round Robin: Similar to SCHED_FIFO, but threads of identical priority receive fixed time slices to prevent a single thread from monopolizing execution on a core.

topic.para: In production real-time environments, there are three primary ways to set these policies depending on whether control belongs to the system administrator, a startup script, or the developer:

listitem.para: Persistently using &systemd; unit files: The policy is set in a .service unit file. For details, refer to .
Temporary using chrt: For details, refer to .
Programmatically within the application code: Real-time applications can configure their own policies internally using POSIX API calls.
